_about: Room shapes and house programmes for room_solver.py. Sizes in squares (1 m). Lookup tables: edit the numbers, not the code.

kinds._about: side: shortest side of each rectangle; area: [min, max] m2 (the hall and landing: their passage only, not the stairs); target: the size aimed for; aspect: longest side over shortest at most; l: may be an L of two rectangles; grow: may be stretched past its largest size when the house has more floor than its rooms; window: need / want / no; small_window: its window needs only its own square on the wall, not one either side (a small window by a partition); cap: windows at most; from: rooms its door may open from (in the order of preference); build: Build's room kind cupboard: 1-2 squares (under the stairs, the airing cupboard, a built-in wardrobe): every programme may use a few to tidy odd squares. shop_floor: a shop's sales floor (Build names it after the shop's use: _assign_shop_floor); stockroom: behind it; flat_hall: a flat's own hall, its front door off the shared landing. openplan: a small flat's living room with its kitchen in it. flat_zone: a block of flats' first stage - the floor a flat will have (room_solver.solve_flats), then laid out as a flat_unit of its own. store: a block of flats' communal store (bins, bikes, the cleaner's cupboard), filling what no flat can use. Commercial rooms (the "shops" table below): use: front / back = the room is named after the business's own use (uses.py: the pizza place's dining room and kitchen) in place of build; frontage: its street wall is the glazed shop front (or a pub's front) with its door in the middle; street_door: its own door from the street in an ordinary wall (a surgery's waiting room).

rules._about: 1990 UK rules the code checks. bedrooms_ground: storeys a house must have before its bedrooms all go upstairs. no_door: pairs that never share a door (building regulations: no WC straight off a kitchen). pitch: window spacing on the front and back, and on the ends.
rules._behind: behind: [a, b] = a is further from the street than b (its middle). larger: [a, b] = every a bigger than every b. "main" is the main bedroom.
rules._prefer_from: prefer_from: the room a kind would rather open from; a programme room's own prefer wins (the hall to the kitchen in council houses, detached houses and bungalows, not through the lounge; a Victorian kitchen through the back room).
rules._programme: programme_by_area: Build's pick when the sub-type gives none - two storeys: the first programme whose ground floor is under its m2; one storey: bungalow.
rules._period: period_styles: palette styles whose large houses are period ones (and every listed kit style, with __ in its name).
rules._bath_size: Every room Build furnishes as a bathroom (bathroom, wc, ensuite) is at least 2 x 2 squares; a bathroom at least 3 x 2 (6 m2) for a bath, toilet, sink and cupboard (user, 2026-10-20).
rules._storeys: programme_by_storeys: three or more storeys - a period style is townhouse_period (period_large over its m2), else townhouse_modern (executive_large over its m2).
rules._look: look_programmes: each 1993 look (Building_types subtypes.look_of) to its programme for a two-storey house; null = not for the room solver (flats: Build's own). choose_programme then takes one storey to a bungalow, three or more to a town house, and a ground floor of townhouse_large_m2 or more to a large house. period_looks: looks whose large houses are period ones. habitable: the kinds an EPC counts as habitable rooms.
rules._shops: Homes over shops: shop_house (one home: a house's rooms above, a maisonette over two floors), shop_flats (a flat a floor), shop_flats2 (two flats a floor), by the building's homes (knox_homes) and storeys. unit on a room: which flat it is in; a room opens only from its own flat (a flat_hall from the landing). Each falls back to fewer homes when its homes do not fit (two flats a floor, then one, then one home over the shop).
rules._flats: A block of flats (shops.py's flats): stage 1 a floor's shared hall or landing and stairs and a zone for each flat (its homes over its storeys, 2-4 a floor), the zones the same on every floor of the same outline; stage 2 each zone a flat_unit. Fewer flats a floor when they do not fit. Each floor its own count: no more flats than its floor gives flat_split_m2 each.

weights._about: Objective costs. stair_room: per m2 of hall or landing passage (keep the rooms with stairs as small as possible). stretch: per m2 a room is stretched past its kind's largest size (so a house with more floor than rooms takes another room before a 47 m2 bedroom). epc_rooms: per habitable room more or fewer than the house's EPCs say it has. window_stack_ground (a programme's own weights): windows over the ground floor's (0 over a shop front). store: per m2 of a block's communal store (so a flat takes the floor when it can).

programmes._about: Each programme is a list of variants tried in order. A variant is one list of rooms per storey (ground first). A room: kind; front / back = squares of that wall it must have; main = the main bedroom (on the front); prefer = the room it would rather open from; optional = there if it fits (each one there is worth weights.optional_room, or its own value), so one variant serves a small house and a big one. area on a room: its own [min, max] m2. root: the room the storey's doors start from, in place of a hall. from: its own list of rooms it may open from. A programme may instead be {"variants": [...], "weights": {...}, "kinds": {kind: {...}}}: its own weights and room sizes (a large house's bigger rooms, a hall and landing that may be corridors). A variant is tried only on a house with as many storeys as it has. flat_unit: one flat, solved in its zone (entry: its hall holds the square its front door opens onto). flats_block: made by room_solver.solve_flats, not listed here.

shops._about: Commercial ground floors. A business's use (uses.py: front room, back room) falls in a class by its front room (classes; anything else is retail), and the class gives its ground floor (grounds). A programme named base@class is the base programme with its ground floor's shop rooms swapped for the class's (shop_house@food: a takeaway with a home over it); shop_only@class is a business with no homes: its ground floor, a stair hall behind the shop when it has an upper floor (stair_from: the rooms it opens from; no street door of its own), and the class's upper floors (uppers by class, else store: store rooms and a break room). stair_hall: that hall (at the back of the shop). rear: k on a room = k squares of the back wall (else a side wall) wanted, at weights.rear (a unit with party walls all round has no back wall; back: k would make it impossible); rear_need: needed where the building has such a wall (a pub cellar's drop door). upper_extra: added to each floor of homes over a business that is not a plain shop (the business's own store rooms; else a big floor's flat is stretched). A pub has a gents and a ladies (licensed premises), and may have a snug or games room off a bar. Its last three cupboards (value 0: no reward for being there) fill the corners a turned building's stepped outline leaves, too narrow for a bar (the White Horse, Alton: without them no layout in the time). A programme room's own use (false: none) wins over its kind's (a pub's kitchen stays a kitchen). Pubs: pub_uk.py.

converted._about: Option C: an office, surgery or guest house in a building whose look is a house's (rules.look_programmes, or a period house cut into flats: looks) is laid out as the house it is (choose_programme), then its rooms are renamed by its class (rename: a house kind to a game room, or front / back = the use's own: a dentist's consulting rooms). With homes over the business only the ground floor is renamed, except where all_floors (a guest house: the owners' bedroom stays theirs). No glazed shop front and no fascia (a solicitor's in a Georgian house).
